_doc: The landscape (sim/nature, api/nature_loader.cpp). elements: the brush of small things: its limits and kinds are modelling choices of the game, area_m2 the area its density is per; the kinds before first_effect are things laid on the ground (render/cover element models), from it effects (render/element_effects.gd). weather: limits and defaults. wind 0-30 m/s reaches Beaufort 11 (28.5-32.6 m/s, WMO No. 8 annex). rain and thunder are shares; lightning, strikes a minute. current 0-4 m/s: a modelling choice. mist_height_m and gully_auto are modelling choices. clouds: span_m the sky's period (10 240 m, the largest map the medium town fills), height_m the cumulus base (the lifting condensation level seen over a city, 32-960 m as the tool allows), size_m and density modelling choices compared with reference-minha photos. fog: height_m from 2 m, the top of shallow fog (AMS Glossary; WMO code table 0-20-003), to 160 m, a modelling choice, fog_texel_m the window's texel. paint: kinds in the card order of the Ground tab; strength_scale turns the brush's percent into a dab; rock_reach the rock laid past a landform's dab so it reaches the foot of its cliff (modelling). trees: density per hectare comes from the brush; models are two oaks, two cypresses, two palms. ecology: formations are densities 0..1 of each stratum, written from the field descriptions of the fitofisionomias (IBGE, Manual Tecnico da Vegetacao Brasileira, 2012; Ribeiro & Walter 2008 for the cerrado) as modelling choices, except where a tree cover is published: cerradao 50-90 % (closed_canopy plus trees 0.9, its dense end) and cerrado denso and tipico 20-70 % (trees 0.45, the middle), both Ribeiro & Walter as quoted in the works listed in ports/landscape/research.md; caatinga has no clear dominance of trees and is thick with cacti and spiny shrubs (IBGE 2012); riparian_near and far the strip of forest along water, a modelling choice round the 30 m of Lei 12.651/2012 art. 4 I a (not read for this port); flat and steep degrees: the relief classes of Embrapa (Santos et al., Sistema Brasileiro de Classificacao de Solos): flat fades between 8 % (4.6 degrees, the top of suave ondulado) and 20 % (11.3, the top of ondulado), steep rises from 45 % (24.2, the top of forte ondulado) to 75 % (36.9, the start of escarpado); forest_line the altitude the high grasslands start at, scaled to this map's relief.

styles._doc: What the regional style of a city changes in the landscape: the flora of its climate. Sun, sky and light are physical and do not change. Until the style lives in the CityState the loader reads roadcraft.

mixes._doc: Each key is a share or a distance in the mix of a biome's communities (sim/nature/ecology.cpp). Where each community stands comes from the field descriptions; the number that turns a description into a smooth edge has no published value and is a modelling choice, stated here by group. vereda_*: veredas lie on flat, wet valley floors by the water (Ribeiro & Walter 2008): deep, patch and the 24-128 m from water are modelling choices for 'valley floor by a stream'. dense_*: cerradao on the lower ground and in patches of better soil: modelling choices. rupestre_*: campo rupestre on ridges and sandstone (Ribeiro & Walter 2008): modelling choices. cerrado_floor: the share of cerrado always kept, so a mix never sums to nothing: modelling choice. ridge_altitude_m, patch_altitude_m: how far a ridge and a patch move the forest line, scaled to this map's relief: modelling choices. varzea_*: forest on ground the rivers flood, the 16-88 m strip scaled to the map's rivers: modelling choices. caatinga_ridge, pampa_ridge: rock showing on crests: modelling choices. capao_*: forest islands in hollows of the pampa, along water at capao_riparian: modelling choices. low_*: the flooded lowland of the pantanal: modelling choices. cordilheira_*, pantanal_*: cordilheiras are forest on old levees 1-2.5 m high, the islands between flooded fields (Nhecolandia studies, see ports/landscape/research.md), so they take the patches and yield on low ground; the shares are modelling choices. ragged_*, shrub_*: how much the fine patch frays the canopy and the shrubs, against the bare mix: modelling choices.
